items.title: Amherst community rallies around father and son critically injured in highway accident in Mississauga, Ontario
items.summary: Y. (WKBW) — A father and son from Amherst are fighting to recover from catastrophic injuries after a highway accident in Canada left both of them with life-altering trauma, and neighbors and friends are stepping up to help. On Aug. 11, 43-year-old Masud Biswas and his youngest son, 12-year-old Marif Biswas, were involved in a minor collision with another vehicle on Highway 403 in Mississauga, Ontario. When they stepped out onto the highway shoulder to inspect the damage and exchange insurance information, a third vehicle veered off course and slammed into one of the cars, which then struck both father and son, causing catastrophic injuries. m. Masud and Marif were struck a short time later and taken to trauma centers. Both of Masud's legs have been amputated above the knee, and he continues his recovery at ECMC. Marif, a 7th grader at Amherst Middle School, has undergone multiple surgeries as doctors work to save his legs. He remains at Golisano Children's Hospital of Buffalo. The family's next-door neighbor, Matt Higgins, and his family have launched a GoFundMe campaign to help cover mounting medical and living expenses. items.title: Woman arrested for attempted murder following stabbing in Mississauga
items.summary: A 42-year-old woman has been arrested and charged after a man was stabbed outside a shelter in Mississauga over the weekend. m. in the area of Main Street and Dundas Street East, east of Dixie Road. When officers arrived, they found a man suffering from a serious stab wound to the neck. Paramedics told CP24 they performed life-saving measures before the man was taken to hospital, where he remains in critical condition. Initially, police say they arrested a man who was involved in a altercation with the victim. He has since been released. “As the investigation progressed, officers determined that he was not responsible for the stabbing and he was subsequently released,” police said in a statement. Police then identified 42-year-old Lorena Sanchez of Mississauga as a suspect, who allegedly fled the area prior to police arrival. On Monday, police arrested and charged Sanchez with one count of attempted murder.

items.title: Labour Day Toronto and Ontario cities: What’s Open and Closed
items.summary: This year, Labour Day falls on Sept. 7, 2026, in Mississauga, Brampton, Toronto, Hamilton, Oakville, Milton, Burlington, Oshawa, Whitby, Pickering, Clarington, Niagara Falls and the Niagara Region. While government buildings, services and many businesses/stores will be closed on Monday, some places will remain open. However, to avoid disappointment, it’s best to call ahead or check online to confirm if your favourite restaurant or local grocery store is open. Here’s what’s open and closed in southern Ontario towns and cities on Labour Day: Square One Shopping Centre is open, along with Walmart Supercentre, The Rec Room and The Food District. Whole Foods Square One and T&T Supermarket are also open. Residents and visitors can also visit Celebration Square and the Celebration Square fountain, Rabba grocery stores, select Beer Store locations, the YMCA health and fitness centre in Mississauga, restaurants, cafes, and bars that are typically open on Mondays (call ahead to confirm), the Mississauga Chinese Centre, and movie theatres. On Sept. 7, non-emergency federal, provincial, municipal (including City Hall), and Region of Peel offices will be closed. Banks, libraries and some community centres will also be closed. Canada Post will be closed (no mail pickup or delivery), and there will be no waste collection on Labour Day. Garbage and recycling will be picked up one day later than usual, and Community Recycling Centres will also be closed. items.title: Police Call Mississauga Stabbing an Isolated Incident as Search for Second Suspect Continues
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel Regional Police say the Mississauga stabbing that left one person fighting for their life is believed to be an isolated incident with no ongoing threat to public safety. The outlet reports one suspect was taken into custody at the scene while officers continued searching the surrounding area for a second suspect. INsauga reports police describe the outstanding suspect as a Hispanic woman in her mid-30s, approximately five-foot-four, with blonde and brown hair. According to the outlet, the victim remained in critical condition at a trauma centre as of the latest police update. INsauga reports officers remained in the Main Street and Dundas Street East area as the investigation continued.

items.title: Mississauga aims to secure over $401M in funding for housing support infrastructure
items.summary: Ontario students can expect a mix of sun and cloud on Tuesda… City staff are backing the proposal for the 3-acre Dixie sit… If approved, the funding will support two transit projects including a new Transit Mobility Hub. 4 million from the provincial and federal governments, with that money going toward housing and transit infrastructure. 4 million from the federal and provincial governments to support housing and transit infrastructure, officials announced on Sept. 3. The funding comes through the Development Charges Reduction Program, part of the Canada-Ontario Partnership to Build. The initiative supports municipalities that have reduced development charges to spur housing development, according to a city news release. Mayor Carolyn Parrish, Premier Doug Ford and other government officials made the announcement. Mississauga secured the funds after becoming one of the first Ontario cities to cut development charges by 100 per cent for certain types of housing developments to encourage growth. This reduction remains in effect until March 31, 2029.

items.title: Twin 16-Storey Towers Proposed for Dixie Site Head to Planning Committee
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, city staff are recommending council approve a rezoning application that would bring two 16-storey apartment towers to a 3-acre site at 1225 Dundas Street East in the Dixie neighbourhood. The outlet reports the towers would be connected by a six-storey podium and contain a combined 553 residential rental units, along with ground-floor commercial space. Mississauga.com reports the proposal also includes 34 four-storey back-to-back townhouses, bringing the total to 587 residential units. According to the outlet, the site is owned by a group of five investment companies, including Stephen-Mitchell Realty Limited and Whitehorn Investments Limited. Mississauga.com reports a city staff report noted the property sits within a designated intensification area meant to accommodate significant growth, with Mississauga's planning committee set to vote on the application September 8.

items.title: Both Suspects Now in Custody After Stabbing Left Mississauga Man Critically Injured
items.summary: According to CityNews Toronto, Peel Regional Police say both suspects have now been taken into custody after a man was stabbed in Mississauga on Sunday evening. The outlet reports the victim suffered critical injuries and was transported to a trauma centre by paramedics. CityNews Toronto reports one suspect was arrested at the scene while the second, described as a Hispanic woman in her mid-30s, approximately five-foot-four with blonde and brown hair, was taken into custody after a search of the surrounding area. According to the outlet, the large police presence during the search was centred around a nearby homeless shelter. CityNews Toronto reports motorists were advised to use alternate routes while officers worked the scene.

items.title: 32 vehicles broken into in 30 minutes in Mississauga, man wanted
items.summary: Police are on the hunt for a man after more than 30 vehicles were broken into during a 30-minute span in Mississauga. m. m. in the area of Alpha Mills Road, Falconer Drive and Plainsman Road. Investigators said the suspect entered 32 vehicles by smashing windows or accessing those that had been left unlocked. Multiple valuables were stolen, though police did not specify what was taken. All of the vehicles were unoccupied at the time and none were stolen, police said. The suspect is described as a white man, approximately 30 years old with a medium build. He was reportedly wearing a jacket with the word “POLO” written on the back collar, joggers and two-tone shoes with white soles. He was also carrying a backpack. Police are asking anyone with information about the incidents or the suspect to contact 11 Division investigators at 905-453-2121, ext. 1133.

items.title: Police Release Suspect Photos After 32 Vehicle Break-Ins Hit Three Mississauga Streets
items.summary: According to CityNews Toronto, Peel Regional Police have released photos of a suspect wanted in connection with at least 32 vehicle break-ins in Mississauga. The outlet reports the break-ins occurred on September 3 in the Alpha Mills Road, Falconer Drive and Plainsman Road areas. CityNews Toronto reports all of the vehicles were unoccupied at the time and that nothing was taken during the incidents. According to the outlet, the suspect is described as a white man approximately 30 years old with a medium build. CityNews Toronto reports he was last seen wearing a jacket with the word POLO written on the back collar, joggers, and two-toned shoes with a white sole, while carrying a backpack.

items.title: Square One, Celebration Square Among Mississauga Spots Staying Open Over Labour Day
items.summary: According to INsauga, several Mississauga businesses and attractions will remain open on Labour Day, September 7, even as most government offices and services close for the holiday. The outlet reports Square One Shopping Centre will be open, along with Walmart Supercentre, The Rec Room, The Food District, Whole Foods Square One and T&T Supermarket. INsauga reports Celebration Square and its fountain, select Rabba grocery stores and Beer Store locations, the city's YMCA health and fitness centre, and the Mississauga Chinese Centre will also be open, alongside movie theatres and many restaurants, cafes and bars. According to the outlet, Mississauga City Hall and Region of Peel offices will be closed for the day, along with banks, libraries and some community centres, and there will be no Canada Post pickup or delivery. INsauga reports garbage and recycling collection will be pushed back one day, MiWay will run on a regular Sunday schedule, and GO Transit will operate on a Saturday schedule.

items.title: MiWay Drops Route 110A as University Express Service Ramps Up for the School Year
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, MiWay is adjusting its bus schedule starting Tuesday, September 7, increasing service on some of its busiest corridors as students return to school. The outlet reports the changes include more frequent service on Route 110 University Express, which connects downtown Mississauga, the University of Toronto Mississauga campus, the Erin Mills community and Clarkson GO Station. Mississauga.com reports MiWay will discontinue its Route 110A University Express as part of the increased service on the main route. According to the outlet, two other routes will see reduced service due to lower ridership. Mississauga.com reports the schedule changes are also timed to resume regular school-day bus runs alongside the start of the new academic year.
